pattern: Local inventory under a geographic promise: precompute 'who can serve this place' as a geo lookup, serve stock from a CDC-fed in-memory copy, keep the authoritative conditional decrement in one shard per location, and treat matching couriers as a batched assignment over a live location index.

tips.nudge: A customer opens the app at home. What must the first screen get right?
tips.hint: Add a functional requirement for showing what can actually be delivered to this address.
tips.show: F1: Show the items available for delivery to the customer's address, from warehouses that can reach it within 30 minutes.

tips.nudge: What turns a cart into a delivery?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for placing an order and paying.
tips.show: F2: Place an order for a cart of items and pay; the order is fulfilled by one warehouse.

tips.nudge: The bag is packed. Who takes it, and how is that decided?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for assigning orders to drivers.
tips.show: F3: Assign each order to a driver who picks it up at the warehouse and delivers it.

tips.nudge: Two customers buy the last bottle of milk. What must not happen?
tips.hint: State a non-functional requirement for inventory correctness at order time.
tips.show: N1: No overselling: an order is confirmed only if every item is in stock at its warehouse (strong consistency per warehouse); browsing may be seconds stale.

tips.nudge: What is the product's promise, and what does the app need to feel instant?
tips.hint: Add non-functional requirements for the delivery promise and availability latency.
tips.show: N2: Availability reads p99 < 100 ms; N3: deliveries within ~30 minutes, so only warehouses within ~30 min travel serve an address.

tips.nudge: Start from daily users and how often they look at items.
tips.hint: read_qps = DAU × views per user / 86,400 s.
tips.show: availability_qps = 10M × 20 / day ≈ 2,300 /s (peak ×5 ≈ 12k /s).

tips.nudge: How many orders per day?
tips.hint: order_qps = orders per day / 86,400 s, with an evening peak.
tips.show: order_qps = 500k / day ≈ 6 /s (peak ×5 ≈ 30 /s): tiny. The hard part is correctness, not volume.

tips.nudge: Warehouses × SKUs per warehouse: is that big?
tips.hint: inventory rows = warehouses × SKUs; × bytes per row.
tips.show: inventory_size = 500 warehouses × 5k SKUs × 100 B ≈ 250 MB: fits in memory, so cache all of it.

tips.nudge: Every active driver reports where they are. How often, and how many drivers?
tips.hint: updates/s = active drivers / seconds between pings.
tips.show: driver_location_qps = 20k drivers / 5 s ≈ 4,000 /s.

tips.nudge: What does the app ask for on the home screen?
tips.hint: A GET with the delivery location (and category/search) returning available items.
tips.show: GET /availability?lat=&lng=&category= → {warehouse_ids, items[{sku, name, price, in_stock}]}

tips.nudge: What does checkout send, and how do you make a retry safe?
tips.hint: A POST with the cart lines, address and payment token, plus an idempotency key.
tips.show: POST /orders {lines[{sku, qty}], address, payment_token} + Idempotency-Key → 201 {order_id, warehouse_id, eta} | 409 out of stock

tips.nudge: Stock lives somewhere specific. What is the key?
tips.hint: One row per (warehouse, SKU) with a quantity you can decrement safely.
tips.show: inventory(warehouse_id, sku, qty, version) PK (warehouse_id, sku) in Postgres, sharded by warehouse.

checks.label: Nearby availability designed as its own part

tips.nudge: 'What can I get delivered here?' joins geography and stock. Give it its own part.
tips.hint: Compare computing distances per request with precomputed service areas per geo cell, and DB reads with an in-memory copy of stock.
tips.show: Part 'Nearby availability': geohash cell → warehouses within 30 min (precomputed isochrones) in Redis; stock per warehouse cached in Redis, kept fresh by CDC events.

checks.label: Order placement without overselling designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Two orders race for the last unit. Treat that as its own sub-problem.
tips.hint: Compare check-then-write, Redis counters, and a conditional decrement inside a DB transaction.
tips.show: Part 'Order placement': one Postgres transaction on the warehouse shard: UPDATE inventory SET qty = qty - :n WHERE warehouse_id=:w AND sku=:s AND qty >= :n for every line, plus the order row; any line fails → roll back → 409.

checks.label: Driver assignment designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Many orders, many drivers, a 30-minute promise. Give matching its own part.
tips.hint: Compare greedy nearest-driver at order time with batched matching every few seconds per warehouse.
tips.show: Part 'Dispatch': drivers report GPS to a Redis GEO index; a dispatcher consumes OrderConfirmed events and matches ready-soon orders to nearby idle drivers in short batches, then offers the job by push.

checks.label: Read path can absorb the read load

tips.nudge: Availability is read ~1,000 times per order. Where should those reads go?
tips.hint: Put an in-memory copy in front of the inventory database.
tips.show: Redis: geo cell → warehouses, and stock per (warehouse, SKU), updated from CDC.

tips.nudge: Customers and drivers both call you. What spreads that traffic?
tips.hint: Stateless services behind something that distributes requests.
tips.show: Load balancer / API gateway in front of availability, order, location and tracking services.

tips.nudge: No customer request decides which driver goes. What does?
tips.hint: Add a component dedicated to assignment.
tips.show: A dispatcher worker that consumes confirmed orders and assigns drivers from the location index.

checks.label: Stock taken by unpaid orders handled

tips.nudge: Stock is decremented, then the card is declined. What now?
tips.hint: Decide the order of 'take stock' and 'charge card', and how you undo one if the other fails.
tips.show: Decrement first (pending_payment), then authorize; on decline or timeout run a compensating increment; a sweeper releases pending orders older than 10 min. Capture only after packing.

checks.label: Freshness of what customers see decided

tips.nudge: The cache says 1 left; the database says 0. Is that a bug?
tips.hint: Decide how stale availability may be and what protects correctness.
tips.show: Cache fed by CDC is ~1 s behind; that's acceptable because the order's conditional decrement is the real check. Show 'only a few left' instead of exact counts.

checks.label: Bottlenecks and single points of failure named

tips.nudge: Saturday 9 pm, one warehouse near a stadium. What saturates first?
tips.hint: Walk the order and dispatch paths for one busy warehouse.
tips.show: Drivers at a busy warehouse (the real constraint), hot SKUs on one warehouse shard, the Redis availability cache, and the maps/routing API quota.

tips.nudge: How do you know you're breaking the 30-minute promise before customers complain?
tips.hint: List metrics for availability, orders and delivery.
tips.show: Availability p99 and cache lag, 409 out-of-stock rate at checkout, order → assignment time, ETA error, on-time delivery %, idle vs busy drivers per warehouse.
